clue.text: Ricochets coming closer — cavalrymen run away

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its final letter, so take the end of the word coming
away tells us the run abbreviation is sent off from the cavalrymen

parts.note: lancers are cavalry soldiers armed with lances
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Bullets bounce about as the enemy draws near and the mounted troops flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming closer' reads as approaching, but it means the last letter of 'coming'. 'away' removes R from LANCERS, leaving LANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that glances off a surface strikes it obliquely and bounces away, as a ricochet does.

clue.text: Ealing production that's good-humoured

indicators.note: a production is something made or staged, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A film from the Ealing studio is cheerful in tone.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing Studios in London made famous comedies, which is why 'production' sits so naturally beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a warm, friendly, cheerful person is described as genial.

clue.text: A community centre did command performance of early music

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, here from community

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered

explanation.surface: A local hall staged a royal command performance of early music.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the nine-letter 'community' is U.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a piece of music or poem for dawn, the early morning, so it is literally early music.

clue.text: Old queen united with dogs coming round for talks

indicators.note: the dogs encircle the other pieces, which sit inside them

parts.note: collies are a breed of sheepdog
Q is an abbreviation for queen, as on playing cards
U is a common abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch joins her dogs, who gather around her for conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquies are formal conversations or discussions, so the word is a synonym for talks.

clue.text: 1 across at first supporting very fine capital

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil leads
the numeral one looks like the letter I

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of the word across

explanation.surface: A reference to the first across clue, apparently backing a very fine capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' looks like a cross-reference to GLANCES, but it is I plus the first letter of 'across', which in a down entry go beneath SO and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Golfer's shot home help

definitions.meaning: a golfer whose chip from off the green drops into the hole has pitched it in
to join in and lend a hand with a shared task

explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is both a lofted golf shot that is holed and an idiom for lending a hand.

clue.text: Dolly's for females inside temple

indicators.note: inside tells us the females go within Dolly's surname

parts.note: Dolly Parton is the American country singer; the 's stands for has
a hen is a female bird, as in hen party for women

explanation.surface: Dolly Parton's women-only temple, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the famous ancient temple to Athena on the Acropolis in Athens.

clue.text: Starters for ten — university challenges kitchen to provide food

indicators.note: the starters of words are their first letters, here of the next four words

explanation.surface: A quiz show's opening question tests a college kitchen's ability to feed people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter for ten' is the opening question on University Challenge, a long-running British TV quiz for university teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British school slang for food, especially sweets and snacks, as in a tuck shop.

clue.text: Dances in show done up the pole

indicators.note: up the pole is British slang for crazy or confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dances performed in a show that ended up on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoedowns are lively American square dances or social gatherings with folk dancing.

clue.text: Yuan finally extracted from curious Cantonese wallet

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the remaining letters are rearranged
extracted from means a letter is pulled out of the word Cantonese
finally means take the last letter of the word Yuan

explanation.surface: Chinese currency is pulled out of an odd Cantonese purse.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing N, the end of 'Yuan', from CANTONESE leaves CATONESE, which 'curious' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A notecase is an old British word for a wallet holding banknotes.

clue.text: Explosive chap who must retire for the good of France

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the French words are read backwards

parts.note: le bon is French for the good

explanation.surface: A man with a temper must step down for France's benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive chap' is Alfred Nobel, who invented dynamite; the surface suggests a hothead.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite, is literally a man associated with explosives.

clue.text: Deal with secret dicky bird

parts.note: deal is a timber term for fir or pine planks

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip on handling a secret with a dodgy informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal with' reads as a verb phrase, but 'Deal' is the softwood timber; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The firecrest is a tiny European songbird related to the goldcrest.

clue.text: Trojan wife for whom Charon made trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: The ferryman of the dead made a crossing for a woman from Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Charon is the ferryman of the Underworld in Greek myth, which suits the voyage the surface implies.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromache was the wife of Hector, the Trojan prince, in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Evil humanoid residing in Windsor Castle

indicators.note: residing in means the letters live inside the words Windsor Castle

explanation.surface: A wicked creature is living in the royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcs are the brutish goblin-like creatures of fantasy fiction such as Tolkien's.

clue.text: French statesman and count protecting European currency

indicators.note: protecting means the count surrounds the European letter

parts.note: a tally is a count or reckoning
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A French politician and a nobleman guarding the euro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' reads as a nobleman, which suits the French statesman, but it is TALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Talleyrand was the French diplomat who served Napoleon and later the restored monarchy.

clue.text: Writer describing calendar somewhere in London

parts.note: the Julian calendar was introduced by Julius Caesar
Barnes is a district of south-west London beside the Thames

explanation.surface: An author writes about a calendar used in some part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Barnes is the English novelist who won the Booker Prize for The Sense of an Ending.

clue.text: Rude sign stops rude bankrupt

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the sign goes inside the second word rude

parts.note: insolent means rude and disrespectful
the V sign, made with two fingers, is an offensive gesture in Britain

explanation.surface: An obscene gesture halts a rude person who has gone broke.
explanation.walkthrough: The V sign, with the back of the hand outward, is a British insult like the middle finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent describes a person or firm unable to pay debts, the same as bankrupt.

clue.text: Thrown cigarette end missing forest resident

indicators.note: thrown means tossed about, so the letters are rearranged
end missing means the last letter of cigarette is dropped

explanation.surface: A discarded cigarette butt is lost by someone living in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end missing' removes the final E, leaving CIGARETT for 'Thrown' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger cat, or oncilla, is a small wild cat of South American forests.

clue.text: Poems representing 21's clue

indicators.note: representing means presenting again, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: 21 across is a Freudian concept of self; with the 's it gives four letters ending in S

explanation.surface: Verses standing for the clue at 21.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of '21's' counts as an S in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclogues are short pastoral poems, such as Virgil's dialogues between shepherds.

clue.text: More and more grain's nicely ground

indicators.note: ground means milled to powder, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Grain is being milled ever more finely.
explanation.definitionFit: Increasingly means to a growing degree, so it says the same as more and more.

clue.text: One required for bingo who may display ID?

definitions.meaning: the person who calls out the numbers at a bingo game
a telephoner whose number shows up on ... ID

explanation.definitionFit: The bingo announcer and anyone making a phone call are both known by the same word.

clue.text: Heavy sleepers oversleep after vacation? Herbal medicine is the answer

indicators.note: vacated words are emptied of their insides, leaving only their outer letters

explanation.surface: A remedy for people who sleep too heavily turns out to be herbal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' sounds like a holiday, but it means emptying: Heavy, sleepers and oversleep lose their middles to give HY, SS and OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic plant of the mint family used in traditional herbal remedies.

clue.text: Freudian concept, say, associated with Oedipus, originally

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of Oedipus

explanation.surface: An idea of Freud's, such as the one linked to Oedipus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freud's model of the mind, the conscious self mediating between id and superego is the ego.

clue.text: Drink from Lombardy you almost ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word you loses its final letter

explanation.surface: You nearly asked for a drink from northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts YOU to YO, and 'ordered' rearranges it with LOMBARDY. 'ordered' reads as requesting a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice.

clue.text: Start working with gel

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on
to gel is to set or become firm

explanation.surface: Begin by applying some hair gel.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning or start.

clue.text: Second-best place for boarding

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: The runner-up spot for getting on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-best' reads as one compound word, but it splits into S and TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus or tram stop is where passengers get on.

clue.text: Lady holding line for legion

indicators.note: holding means the lady wraps around the line

parts.note: a countess is a noblewoman, a titled lady

explanation.surface: A noblewoman holds a line in place of a legion of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legion' looks like a noun for a body of troops, but is the adjective in 'their number is legion'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, legion means very numerous, too many to number.

clue.text: Titan finally falling short

indicators.note: falling short means the phrase stops one letter before its end

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A giant finally comes up short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like an indicator for a last letter, but it is the phrase AT LAST, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was the Titan of Greek myth condemned to hold up the heavens.

clue.text: Chuck and Kitty providing frequent supper

parts.note: to chuck is to toss or throw
a kitty is a pot of pooled money, as in card games

explanation.surface: Two pets supply a regular evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supper' is not an evening meal but one who sups, a drinker; Chuck and Kitty look like names.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a habitual drunkard, someone who drinks often.

clue.text: Jolly fish entered rough water

indicators.note: entered means the fish goes into the jolly

parts.note: a jolly is British slang for a jaunt or outing
the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A cheerful fish swam into choppy water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide rip is a stretch of turbulent sea where currents meet.
